clue.text: Went to see short recording — entertaining plot

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting a guest: one piece holds the other within it
short means the word is cut down to its familiar clipped form

parts.note: a video is a recording
a plot of land is a site

explanation.surface: Someone drops by to watch a brief clip with an absorbing storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a storyline beside 'recording', but it is a building plot; 'short' clips the word to its familiar abbreviated form.
explanation.definitionFit: To have visited a person or place is to have gone along to see them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Odd bits of scum in phial able to be seen

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a vial is a phial, a small bottle

indicators.note: odd bits means the first and third letters of scum

explanation.surface: Visible scum floating in a small glass bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual means relating to sight, so visible, able to be seen.

clue.text: Becomes aware of shilling and other coins

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shilling, the old British coin
cents are coins of other currencies

explanation.surface: Someone notices a shilling among foreign coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent something is to detect it, as a dog picks up a smell, and so become aware of it.

clue.text: Warned of temperature on earth changing — aim to conserve energy

indicators.note: changing means the letters of earth are rearranged
to conserve means the word keeps the extra letter safe inside it

parts.note: an aim is an end, a goal
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A climate warning: temperatures are rising, so try to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' signals the anagram of the planet's name, and 'to conserve' tucks the energy symbol inside the goal word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have threatened is to have menaced or given warning of trouble, a close synonym.

clue.text: Plan day on vessel

parts.note: a raft is a simple floating vessel

explanation.surface: Planning a day out on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough preliminary version of a design or document is a plan, as a noun synonym.

clue.text: Appropriate female posing topless

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter, its top

parts.note: sitting for a portrait is posing for an artist

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a woman modelling without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests nudity but simply removes the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitting is suitable or apt for the occasion, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Neglected roof gent fixed — about time

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
fixed means the letters are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman finally repaired the roof, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges ROOF GENT, and 'about' wraps those letters round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neglected has been left unattended or overlooked, matching a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Goes over summits

definitions.meaning: to top something is to go over it or exceed it

explanation.surface: A climber passes over mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means surpasses or goes above; as a noun plural it means peaks.

clue.text: I am in front of a trap, Edward supposed

indicators.note: in front of means the first piece precedes the next in this down entry

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a gin is a snare or trap
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward assumes he is ahead of a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin is an old word for an animal trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To have imagined something is to have supposed or assumed it to be so.

clue.text: Fattest — most swell

definitions.meaning: great can mean big or bulky, so this is the largest
swell is old slang for excellent, so this is the most excellent

explanation.surface: Two superlatives about size, one swelling more than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means large, and also excellent or swell, so the superlative fits both senses.

clue.text: Guide animal

definitions.meaning: to guide is to direct a course, as with a vehicle
a young castrated bull raised for beef

explanation.surface: Perhaps a guide dog or other helper animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is directing a course; the noun sense is a young bullock raised for beef.

clue.text: A sign of hesitation over uniform one could be taking off

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
plane as an adjective means level or even throughout, so uniform

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates about a uniform, perhaps a pilot's, before departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' tempts you toward the NATO letter U; here it means flat and even, PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is a thing that may at any moment be lifting off a runway, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Draw a trainer, initially with grip

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of trainer is used

parts.note: traction is the grip of a tyre or shoe on a surface

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice on drawing a sports shoe and showing its grippy sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is a crowd-puller, something that appeals, as a top act is a big draw.

clue.text: Prime minister grave and tense

parts.note: a grave is a pit dug in the ground
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A premier described as serious and on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Elder and the Younger were both British prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both William Pitts led British governments in the eighteenth century, so this is an example of a premier.

clue.text: Turn and notice reforms — it's what most leaders want

parts.note: to reel is to spin or turn round

indicators.note: reforms means the letters of notice are shaped anew

explanation.surface: Politicians spin and promise reforms to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting heads of government typically hope to win another term in office, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Cuckoo nestles here, keeping very still

indicators.note: keeping means the scrambled letters hold the other piece inside them
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order

explanation.surface: A cuckoo, famous for using others' nests, sits motionless in one here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' fits the nesting picture but is the anagram signal; 'still' looks like 'motionless' but means 'even so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, used as an adverb, means even so or yet, which matches the conjunctive sense.

clue.text: Learning routine I'd adapted

indicators.note: adapted means the letters are altered into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone describes how they adjusted their study routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is scholarly knowledge, the noun sense of learning.

clue.text: People who mock son about proposals

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
offers are proposals

explanation.surface: A son's suggestions get laughed at by mockers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a containment signal but is C, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to jeer or mock, so those who scoff are mockers.

clue.text: Those who keep people occupied?

parts.note: keeping people occupied sounds like entertaining them, but occupied here means under military occupation

explanation.surface: Sounds like entertainers who keep folk busy.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupying force takes over a country by attack, so those who keep a people under occupation are invaders.

clue.text: Prisoners frequently leaving France because of this

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners

indicators.note: leaving means the letters for France depart from the word frequently

explanation.surface: Convicts often escaping from France for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means as a result or therefore, matching the phrase giving a reason.

clue.text: Want prayers to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word is spoken out loud and sounds like another

parts.note: pleas are prayers, earnest requests

explanation.surface: Someone wishes their prayers to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: As in do as you please, the verb means wish or want.

clue.text: Information's trapping soldiers and politicians

indicators.note: trapping means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: gen is slang for information, and the 's adds an S
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers of the British Army

explanation.surface: Intelligence catching out the army and politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an environmentalist political party, such as the Green Party, are known by this name.

clue.text: Be scared of loud organ

parts.note: F is forte, the music marking for loud
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by a booming church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to be scared of it; the verb fits directly.

clue.text: Crack bone with feather duster?

parts.note: a rib is a bone
a feather duster could tickle, so it is playfully a tickler

explanation.surface: Breaking a bone with a feather duster, an absurd image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like 'break' alongside 'bone', but means a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a wisecrack or joke, and a very funny joke is one that makes you laugh hard.

clue.text: Drive fast, small military vehicles

parts.note: to tank along is informal for driving at speed

explanation.surface: Little army vehicles racing along.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured fighting vehicles on caterpillar tracks are a well-known example of military vehicles.

clue.text: Artist locked up in jail — a delinquent

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top
locked, with in, says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A painter jailed as a young offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locked ... in' hides ILAD in jaIL A Delinquent, and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was a famous Spanish surrealist painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Excitement surrounding leaders in Ebbw Vale getting promotion

indicators.note: surrounding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: elation is joyful excitement

indicators.note: leaders in means the opening letter of each of the two Welsh words

explanation.surface: Someone in the Welsh town of Ebbw Vale thrilled at getting a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebbw Vale is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to a higher rank or position is an elevation, a synonym for promotion.

clue.text: One rodent with tail in snare hacked off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: tail in means the last letter of snare

explanation.surface: A rodent with its tail caught in a trap would be furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked off' is British slang for annoyed, not cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked off is informal British for annoyed or fed up, so a synonym for angry.

clue.text: Uproar's about holding second meeting

indicators.note: holding means the reversed word keeps the extra letter within it
about means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: uproar's read as noise's, the plural of noise

explanation.surface: A meeting descends into an uproar about holding a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NOISES to SESION, and 'holding' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period of meeting, as of a court or council, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bowlers with no power — they do no good

indicators.note: with no means the letter for power is taken away

parts.note: spinners are slow bowlers in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket team's bowlers have lost their power and are useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinners are cricket bowlers who spin the ball slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoers who transgress are described as people who do no good, a cryptic-style definition.
